description: A plant manager must authorize the use of a reclaimed polymer lot for a medical-device housing run and finalize the blend, inspection, storage, waste, and documentation controls, with input from a quality engineer and an environmental compliance specialist.

shared_context.S1: The medical-device housing run is scheduled for Thursday, and the available virgin polymer is insufficient to complete the planned batch.
shared_context.S2: A lot of reclaimed polymer pellets is available in the materials cage and has not yet been authorized for this product.
shared_context.S3: Mara makes the final authorization decision, and the plant normally records material approval, inspection, storage, waste, and documentation controls before a regulated-product run begins.
shared_context.S4: Plant policy requires quality and environmental-compliance sign-off before any reclaimed material is used in a regulated-product run.

PF1.text: Jon's completed lab review shows the reclaimed polymer is suitable for this housing only at a 15% reclaimed-to-85% virgin blend; he also confirmed that the first 50 molded housings must receive FTIR identity testing, but the lab result has not yet been attached to the production traveler.

PF2.text: Priya's review of the supplier's revised safety data sheet, received late yesterday and not yet entered in the plant's chemical register, classifies the reclaimed lot's additive residue as regulated process waste, requiring labeled segregated storage and a hazardous-waste manifest for any discarded pellets or purge material.

acceptance_conditions: The reclaimed polymer must be authorized at exactly a 15% blend.
The first exactly 50 housings must receive FTIR identity testing.
The reclaimed material must be placed in segregated labeled storage.
Discarded reclaimed pellets or purge material must require a hazardous-waste manifest.
The lab result must be committed for attachment to the production traveler before the run.
The quality finding must be cited by the decision-maker as justification.

content_checks.C6: any('production traveler' in c['detail'] and ('Attach lab result' in c['detail'] or 'Lab result' in c['detail'] or 'lab result' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The lab review changes authorization to a permitted use, fixes the blend at exactly 15%, fixes FTIR testing at exactly the first 50 housings, and requires a traveler-attachment commitment.
The revised safety-data-sheet classification changes storage to segregated labeled storage and changes disposal controls to require a hazardous-waste manifest.
